This stage is a mini-STORM, spawning multiple LLM agent with different perspective and perform multi-round conversation.
The knowledge base (i.e. mind map) will be initialize using the collected information.

nodes.label: generate_report

The article generation follows the paradigm in STORM paper, where it considers mind map nodes as section names, and generate the report section by section.

Returns:

Represents an expert agent in the Co-STORM framework.
The `CoStormExpert` is a specialized type of `Agent` that is tasked with participating in roundtable discussions within the Co-STORM system.
The expert uses language models to generate action plans, answer questions, and polish its utterances based on the current conversation history and knowledge base.

nodes.label: SimulatedUser
nodes.docstring:
Simulated Users is a special type of Agent in Co-STORM that simulates real user interaction behavior based on the given intent.

This class can be used for automatic experiments.
For more information, please refer to Section 3.4 of Co-STORM paper: https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2408.15232

nodes.label: Moderator
nodes.docstring:
The moderator's role in the Co-STORM framework is to inject new perspectives into the conversation to avoid stagnation, repetition, or overly niche discussions.
This is achieved by generating questions based on unused, uncited snippets of information retrieved since the last moderator's turn.
The selected information is reranked according to its relevance to the conversation topic and its dissimil

nodes.label: PureRAGAgent
nodes.docstring:
PureRAGAgent only handles grounded question generation by retrieving information from the retriever based on the query.
It does not utilize any other information besides the query itself.

It's designed for Co-STORM paper baseline comparison.

nodes.label: WriteSection
nodes.docstring:
Write a single Wikipedia article section using the provided source material.

Formatting requirements:
1. Begin with the section heading using '#', '##', '###', etc. for the appropriate depth.
2. Inline-cite every factual claim using bracket notation, e.g. [1], [2], [3].
3. Do not add a References or Sources section at the end.

nodes.label: WriteLeadSection
nodes.docstring:
Compose a Wikipedia-style lead section for the article.

The lead must:
1. Stand alone as a concise, self-contained overview of the topic.
2. Establish context, explain the topic's significance, and surface major controversies.
3. Consist of no more than four well-crafted paragraphs.
4. Include inline citations where appropriate (e.g. "The capital is Washington, D.C.[1][3]").

nodes.label: AskQuestion
nodes.docstring:
You are an experienced Wikipedia writer chatting with a subject-matter expert
to gather information for the article you are writing. Ask focused, relevant questions
one at a time. When you have no further questions, say exactly:
"Thank you so much for your help!" to close the conversation.
Do not repeat questions you have already asked.

say exactly: "Thank you so much for your help!" to end the conversation.
Do not repeat questions you have already asked.

Every claim should be traceable to the provided sources. If the gathered information
is insufficient, say so clearly and explain what is missing rather than speculating.
